```python
def f(s):
    rev = s[::-1]
    k = (len(s) + 1) // 2
    t = rev[:k] + 'I' + rev[k:]
    return ' '.join(t.split()[::-1])
```

[DESCRIPTION]: The function takes a string, reverses the entire string character by character, then inserts the character `I` at index `ceil(len/2)` (i.e., `(len+1)//2`). Finally, it reverses the order of the whitespace-separated words (collapsing any runs of whitespace and dropping leading/trailing whitespace, joining with single spaces). Net effect for normal single-spaced input: each word's letters are reversed in place (word order preserved), with an `I` inserted at the position corresponding to the middle of the original string (measured in the fully-reversed string).
